state_key_comparison.results_match: Both win turn, kept hand, seat and first3 agree at both seeds.

findings: Dominant runtime is batch.evaluate_keep (mulligan simulation), not actual gameplay.
Shared physical slot seeds do not reuse evaluation work.
Every variant undergoes independent full London stage evaluations and clears caches.
At keep4 seed0, v1 evaluates two 7-card stages, then 6, 5 and 4-card stages.
Bottom candidates screened: 1 for keep7, 7 for keep6, up to 12 for keep5 and keep4; each uses eight sampled future outcomes at beam60, plus possible refinements at 16 samples.
Database checkpoint and trace summaries are not the bottleneck.
Historical seven-arm N1024 shard 0 completed 16 seeds in ~69m 47s, so the baseline was expensive too; these are different seeds/decks and not an apples-to-apples speed comparison.
next_steps: Instrument per-bottom candidate and future rollout cache hit rates.
Implement stable slot-based RNG for mulligan hypothetical draws and trace each dependency.
Cache/share only exact identical rollout states or reuse validated action certificates; no reuse inferred merely from changed card being absent from opening seven.
Preserve assertive threshold and bottom choice with bit-for-bit parity on fixed seeds before scaling.
Compare CPU/wall time with N16 paired holdout before selecting faster policy.
Parallel shards improve wall clock, not CPU cost.
